title: LynxGrid compliance & ops discovery
topics: Audit logs, SIEM integration and retention
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
summary: Intro call to understand LynxGrid's security requirements for an LLM inference provider. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for a production pilot in Q3 2026. Key concerns: SOC2 scope, customer-managed KMS, audit log retention and SIEM integration, SSO + SCIM for provisioning, fine-grained RBAC, and data residency. Redwood AE and SE presented high-level capabilities, answered questions about key management options and audit hooks, and agreed next steps to exchange security artifacts and run a short benchmark + security questionnaire.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Alright thanks everyone for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this one. We've got Liam from our solutions engineering team, and we have Priya, Evan and Jules from LynxGrid. Can you all hear me okay?
[00:07] Priya Raman: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:11] Liam Ortega: Hi, all. I'll jump into ops and infra questions as we go.
[00:15] Evan Hall: Thanks — short agenda for us is compliance constraints and deployment options, mostly.
[00:19] Maya Chen: Great — quick round, then we'll dig into SOC2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS. We also want to capture any hard blockers so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:29] Priya Raman: To orient you — we're an energy analytics platform working with grid operators; we process telemetry and some customer PII in derived datasets. Our security org is strict, they want proof of encryption and auditability. We're targeting a Q3 pilot for a recommendation engine.
[00:42] Maya Chen: Understood. Quick question on regulatory: is there a data residency requirement? Regions?
[00:46] Evan Hall: All US right now, but some customers require data to remain in us-east or us-west regions. We may need region pinning.
[00:53] Liam Ortega: We support region routing and can pin requests to a region in both Hosted and Dedicated. For Private, obviously customer controls the data plane.
[01:02] Jules Marquez: SOC2 — do you have Type II? And what's the scope? We need audit artifacts for our procurement team.
[01:09] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, we can share the report under NDA. Scope typically covers the control plane and our hosted services; Dedicated and Private have different artifacts — for Private, customers run the data plane so controls differ. We'll share the SOC2 report and our compliance matrix.
[01:24] Priya Raman: Okay — and ISO? Some of our partners ask for ISO-27001 cert.
[01:28] Maya Chen: We're ISO-in-progress; we have controls mapped but not certified globally yet. We'll include the current gap tracker in the docs.
[01:34] Evan Hall: KMS question — we want customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption. Is AWS KMS with bring-your-own-key supported?
[01:41] Liam Ortega: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support CMK and HSM-backed keys. For Hosted there's an option for subscription-level CMKs in certain plans — we can detail the differences. Note the Hosted path using customer-managed KMS is available in enterprise tiers with a limited set of regions.
[01:56] Jules Marquez: How about database-level encryption? We need assurance that model caches, KV cache, and log data are encrypted at rest.
[02:03] Liam Ortega: Absolutely — KV cache and local checkpoints are encrypted. In Dedicated we offer volume-level encryption with CMK; for Hosted we use provider-managed keys by default unless CMK is enabled.
[02:13] Priya Raman: Audit logs: retention and export. We want two things — high-fidelity request/response logs for a subset of calls, and a full access/audit trail for admin activities, exportable to our SIEM. What's the retention window and export options?
[02:26] Maya Chen: We have structured audit logs for admin actions and API request metadata. Retention and routing can be configured — default retention is 90 days for hosted, but can be extended to 365+ for enterprise accounts. Exports to S3, or push to Splunk/Datadog/CloudWatch via forwarder are supported. We also stream audit events to customer endpoints for Dedicated/Private.
[02:44] Evan Hall: For the pilot we only need 180 days, but procurement might ask for 7 years for certain logs. Is long-term cold storage available?
[02:51] Liam Ortega: Yes — archived logs can be moved to cold storage buckets under customer control; we'd work with you on retention policy and cost.
[02:58] Jules Marquez: SSO — we use Okta and SAML. We also need SCIM for provisioning. How mature is your IdP integration?
[03:05] Maya Chen: SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC are supported, SCIM provisioning is available for enterprise accounts and maps to our RBAC. We also support different role mappings and groups.
[03:14] Priya Raman: Do you have role separation — i.e., can we deny access to model deployment but allow read-only telemetry?
[03:19] Liam Ortega: Yes — RBAC is fine-grained: admin, developer, auditor, read-only, and custom roles. You can restrict model rollout, key management, and billing to specific groups.
[03:28] Priya Raman: Great. What about change history on rollouts — we need full auditability for who started a rollout, who approved, etc.
[03:35] Maya Chen: Rollout events are recorded in the audit log with actor, timestamp, and diff snapshots where applicable. We surface these in the Console and can deliver the raw events to your SIEM.
[03:44] Evan Hall: Network controls — can we put Redwood in a VPC peering or private link for Dedicated? We prefer no public internet egress for inference traffic.
[03:52] Liam Ortega: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; Private gives you a customer-managed data plane in your VPC or on-prem. Hosted uses standard public endpoints but can be fronted via private link for certain enterprise engagements.
[04:05] Jules Marquez: Any certifications around hardware HSMs for key storage? We have an HSM requirement for some customers.
[04:10] Liam Ortega: We support HSM-backed KMS providers — the Dedicated and Private options can integrate with Cloud HSM or customer HSMs when deployed on-prem. For Hosted, HSM usage depends on the cloud provider integrations and plan. We'll outline the HSM variants in the security doc.
[04:22] Priya Raman: Data exfil concerns — can you redact or move PII off-model? We do not want raw PII stored by a third party.
[04:29] Maya Chen: We offer per-request redaction hooks and prefix filtering. Additionally, KV cache and prompt caches can be disabled or configured with automatic eviction. For the pilot we can propose a setup that never persists raw inputs to long-term storage, and runs evaluation in a private environment.
[04:45] Evan Hall: Latency vs cost tradeoffs — team wants to know if deduplicating context with prefix cache will alter the data retention model.
[04:53] Liam Ortega: Caching affects short-term KV retention only; caches are secured and can be encrypted with your CMK. Caching reduces per-token cost and usually improves latency. We can configure cache TTLs to match your retention policy.
[05:05] Priya Raman: Do you have a DLP integration or a way to mark certain fields as sensitive so they never persist?
[05:10] Liam Ortega: We have a sensitive-field classifier option and can apply redaction rules pre-ingest. For deeper DLP we can integrate with a partner or pipeline you run pre-send.
[05:19] Maya Chen: Quick callout — I just dropped links in the chat: security questionnaire (https://redwood.app/lynxgrid/sec-q), SOC2 report access (NDA required), and a sample architecture diagram (https://redwood.app/lynxgrid/arch).
[05:31] Jules Marquez: I see the links, thanks. We'll need the SOC2 under NDA. Procurement will also want an indemnity clause draft and cyber insurance limits.
[05:40] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include our standard indemnity language and insurance levels; if you have specific requirements, send them and we'll route to legal.
[05:47] Evan Hall: On the deployment decision: our security team leans toward Dedicated or Private because we want CMK and VPC controls. What are the main operational differences we should expect?
[05:57] Liam Ortega: Operationally Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware in a tenant-isolated pool; you get consistent throughput and we manage software updates. Private is customer-managed data plane — you own the infra patching and networking. Dedicated is faster to stand up; Private gives you the most control for regulated workloads.
[06:13] Priya Raman: Do you offer runbooks and operational playbooks for on-call?
[06:17] Liam Ortega: Yes — Dedicated comes with runbooks, SLOs, and a joint runbook for incident response. Private includes full ops guides for your SREs.
[06:25] Jules Marquez: Is there support for pen testing or red-team exercises against the deployment?
[06:29] Maya Chen: We have a black-box pen test that we can share results for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private, customers can run their own pen tests; we coordinate to ensure scope and safety.
[06:38] Evan Hall: Timeline — if we decide to pilot Dedicated in Q3, what's lead time?
[06:43] Liam Ortega: Typical Dedicated onboarding for a pilot is 4-6 weeks assuming approvals and account provisioning are quick. Private on-prem can be 8-12 weeks depending on hardware and networking windows.
[06:55] Priya Raman: Budget question — is CMK and audit forwarding extra? We need to justify ongoing costs to finance.
[07:02] Maya Chen: CMK and dedicated audit retention are add-ons; we'll provide a pricing sheet. For pilots we can often include a limited CMK trial.
[07:11] Priya Raman: Ok that helps. Jules — any technical asks we missed?
[07:15] Jules Marquez: A few: 1) sample audit log schema, 2) example SCIM mapping, 3) encryption certs for the stack, and 4) evidence of HSM integration if possible.
[07:26] Liam Ortega: We'll attach the audit log sample and SCIM mapping. For HSM evidence, I'll pull a redacted config and vendor info.
[07:34] Maya Chen: Great — recap and next steps. From Redwood: we'll send the SOC2 under NDA, the security questionnaire prefilled, sample audit log schema, SCIM mapping, and a pricing addendum with Dedicated vs Private options. From LynxGrid: provide list of PII fields and any required warranty/insurance thresholds.
[07:52] Evan Hall: Sounds good. Also we'd like a small throughput/latency benchmark for our inference patterns — about 10 concurrent low-latency requests, 256 token windows.
[08:02] Liam Ortega: We can run a short benchmark on Dedicated and Hosted variants — I'll ask for a request trace and sample prompt shapes.
[08:09] Priya Raman: We'll share a sanitized sample set.
[08:12] Maya Chen: Awesome. Anything else? If not, we'll close and send notes.
[08:16] Jules Marquez: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[08:19] Maya Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:22] [meeting end — 46 minutes recorded]
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 report under NDA
Redwood to send filled security questionnaire and audit-log schema
Redwood to provide SCIM/SSO mapping examples and HSM integration notes
Customer to share list of PII fields and sample sanitized prompts for benchmark
Schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff (target: start of Q3)
action_items: Maya Chen - send SOC2 access + security questionnaire (due 2026-06-15)
Liam Ortega - attach audit log schema + SCIM mapping + HSM vendor notes (due 2026-06-18)
Priya Raman - share sanitized sample prompts and PII inventory (due 2026-06-17)
Evan Hall - confirm pilot budget approval and preferred region (due 2026-06-19)
